title: Peanut butter layer cake
subtitle: American three-layer cake with peanut butter frosting
excerpt: A peanut butter layer cake is three deep, lightly sweetened sponge layers filled and frosted with a peanut butter and cream cheese frosting. The sponge is soft and close-crumbed; the frosting is dense and nutty with a faint tang from the cream cheese. A drizzle of chocolate ganache over the finished cake cuts the richness. This is a statement cake that travels well and holds at room temperature for several hours.
sourceNotes: Peanut butter layer cakes are a staple of the American baking tradition, appearing in church cookbooks, diner menus, and Southern food writing from at least the mid-20th century. The cream cheese frosting variant, rather than a pure butter-and-icing-sugar peanut butter frosting, became the standard home baker version from the late 1990s, offering a tang that prevents the frosting from being cloying. The chocolate-ganache drip or drizzle is a later addition, popularised by the 'drip cake' aesthetic of the 2010s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unfrosted sponge layers, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours before frosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the layers a day ahead and store tightly wrapped. Frost on the day of serving.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 180°C or fan 160°C; the layers are ready when a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean

content.text: A peanut butter layer cake delivers a nutty, creamy, slightly salty frosting against a light golden sponge. The cream cheese base keeps the frosting stable at room temperature for several hours and prevents it from being overly sweet. The chocolate drizzle on top is optional but good, it cuts through the richness in every bite.

Preheat the oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Grease and line three 20 cm round cake tins. Cream the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 4 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Add the vanilla. Sift in the flour and baking powder, then fold in with the milk until just combined. Divide evenly among the three tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.

Beat the butter, cream cheese, and peanut butter together until smooth. Sift in the icing sugar and beat on medium speed for 2 minutes until light and creamy. The frosting should hold soft peaks, not stiff, not runny. If it's too soft, refrigerate for 10 minutes before using.

Place one sponge layer on a board or plate. Spread with a generous layer of frosting. Add the second sponge and repeat. Add the third sponge on top. Apply a thin crumb coat of frosting all over and refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm. Apply a final thicker coat and smooth with a palette knife. For the ganache: heat the double cream until just simmering, pour over the chopped dark chocolate, leave for 1 minute, then stir smooth. Cool until slightly thickened, then pour over the top of the cake and let it drip down the sides.
